//: Single Vercel project serving both halves of the app: the React build is served from the CDN, and the Express API runs as one serverless function under /api. Sharing an origin means no CORS round-trip on every request and one URL to remember.
installCommand: cd backend && npm ci --omit=dev && cd ../frontend && npm ci

api/[...slug].js.//: PDF generation is the slowest path; 30s leaves plenty of headroom and stays inside the Hobby plan's limit. includeFiles pulls in assets that are read at runtime by path, which the module tracer cannot see: the Bengali-capable TTFs, and pdfkit's own built-in font metrics.

rewrites.//: Product images are stored in the database and served by the API. The browser asks for /uploads/<file> (the path recorded on the product row); only /api/* can reach a function, so send it there. The Express app is mounted at both paths, so the same URL keeps working on a non-serverless host.
Client-side routing: every non-API path must serve index.html, or a refresh on /products returns 404.

headers.//: This app is a till: it has no reason to read a camera other than for barcode scanning, and no reason to touch location, microphone or payment APIs.
index.html must never be cached, or users keep loading a stale bundle after a deploy.
